findings.issue: “Vitality” substitutes vigor or life-energy for the source’s abundance, prosperity, or well-being. The lexical rationale merely retains an earlier English choice; it does not establish that this narrower assertion represents εὐθηνία. The related flourishing language in II.3 also supports the prosperity/abundance sense.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “having abundance within itself” or “enjoying well-being within itself,” comparing these source-transparent candidates explicitly and updating note e and the lexical decision. The proposed wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅλως ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς
findings.english_quote: and are altogether blinded in their good understanding
findings.issue: “In their good understanding” makes good understanding the sphere of the blindness. The source instead describes blindness that cuts the person off from good understanding; the privative force of ἀπὸ is lost.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “and are completely blinded to good understanding” or “and are completely cut off from good understanding by blindness.” Review the replacement against the entire sentence before adoption.

findings.source_quote: βλέπε οὖν μήποτε παρενθυμηθῇς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην
findings.english_quote: See, then, that you never forget this command.
findings.issue: The warning concerns overlooking or neglecting the command, not merely losing it from memory. Someone can remember a command while disregarding it. Note h acknowledges the broader source sense but retains an English warning that narrows the required response.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Take care, then, never to neglect this command.” Update note h so its explanation supports the revised rendering rather than retention of the earlier wording; submit the replacement for fresh review.

findings.issue: Independently of the standard edition, this wording replaces abundance or well-being with vigor or life-energy. Simplification does not justify that semantic substitution, and the shared metadata supplies retention history rather than a source-based justification.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “with abundance within itself” or an accessible rendering of internal well-being. Compare the candidates directly with εὐθηνία and update the shared note and lexical metadata. Any replacement needs fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅλως ἀποτυφλοῦται ἀπὸ τῆς διανοίας τῆς ἀγαθῆς
findings.english_quote: and they become completely blind in their good understanding
findings.issue: The source describes being blinded away from good understanding. “Blind in their good understanding” instead locates the blindness within understanding still described as good, obscuring the loss expressed by ἀπὸ.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “and they become completely blind to good understanding.” Review this proposed simplified wording directly against the Greek, not merely against a revised standard edition.

findings.source_quote: βλέπε οὖν μήποτε παρενθυμηθῇς τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην
findings.issue: This restricts the warning to memory, whereas the source warns against overlooking or neglecting the command. Remembering it without observing it would satisfy the English instruction but not the source’s warning.
findings.suggested_revision: Consider “Be careful never to neglect this command.” Revise note h accordingly and review the proposed wording afresh.

summary: Both editions cover all fifteen paragraphs and preserve the principal conditions, negations, speakers, household warning, wholehearted repentance, justification declaration, and spirit-departure sequence. Both nevertheless need corrections to three local renderings. Their notes retain the selected working readings while disclosing the reported alternatives, and identify the opening “now” as an editorial insertion. The supplied bounded comparison reports support that disclosure assessment; this review does not authenticate unseen editions or manuscript images, establish exhaustive collation, or certify proposed replacements.
